title: The Most Common Animal With a Backbone Is a Fish You've Never Seen

scenes.text: Earth's most common vertebrate isn't a chicken or a rat.
It's the bristlemouth, a finger-length fish, 3 to 8 centimetres, living 300 to 1,500 metres down in the dark.
Scientists towed nets between 200 and 5,000 metres deep. Up to half of all the fish they caught were bristlemouths.
Roughly one to twelve of them in every washing-machine-sized block of midwater, across every ocean.
Add it up and the estimates run to the trillions, even a quadrillion. A million billion fish.
They glow with tiny lights on their bellies, and every one is born male. The most common backboned animal alive, and you have never seen one.

description:
The most abundant vertebrate on Earth is the bristlemouth, a finger-length deep-sea fish that lives 300 to 1,500 metres down and glows from tiny light organs on its belly.
Trawls in the Atlantic found that 40 to 50 percent of all fish caught were bristlemouths, and estimates of their numbers run to the trillions or even a quadrillion. They are born male and some later become female.
What else is hiding in the deep that we have never seen?
subject: bristlemouth fish
first_comment: A 2014 sonar survey found the deep ocean holds about ten times more fish than anyone thought. Which number here surprised you most?
